verses.zh: 尼八的儿子耶罗波安王十八年，亚比央登基作犹大王，
verses.en: In the eighteenth year of the reign of Jeroboam son of Nebat, Abijah[NOTE:1] became king over Judah.
notes: The Old Greek also has the phrase “the son of Rehoboam.”

verses.zh: 在耶路撒冷作王三年。他母亲名叫玛迦，是押沙龙的女儿。
verses.en: He ruled for three years in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] His mother was Maacah, the daughter of Abishalom.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Abishalom (also in v. 10) is a variant of the name Absalom (cf. 2 Chr 11:20). The more common form is used by TEV, NLT.

verses.zh: 亚比央行他父亲在他以前所行的一切恶，他的心不像他祖大卫的心，诚诚实实地顺服耶和华―他的　神。
verses.en: He followed all the sinful practices of his father before him. He was not wholeheartedly devoted to the Lord his God, as his ancestor David had been.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “his heart was not complete with the Lord his God, like the heart of David his father.”

verses.zh: 然而耶和华―他的　神因大卫的缘故，仍使他在耶路撒冷有灯光，叫他儿子接续他作王，坚立耶路撒冷。
verses.en: Nevertheless for David’s sake the Lord his God maintained his dynasty[NOTE:1] in Jerusalem by giving him a son[NOTE:2] to succeed him[NOTE:3] and by protecting Jerusalem.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “gave him a lamp.”
The Old Greek has the plural “his sons.”
Heb “by raising up his son after him.”
Heb “and by causing Jerusalem to stand firm.”

verses.zh: 因为大卫除了赫人乌利亚那件事，都是行耶和华眼中看为正的事，一生没有违背耶和华一切所吩咐的。
verses.en: He did this[NOTE:1] because David had done what he approved[NOTE:2] and had not disregarded any of his commandments[NOTE:3] his entire lifetime, except for the incident involving Uriah the Hittite.
notes: The words “he did this” are added for stylistic reasons.
Heb “what was right in the eyes of the Lord.”
Heb “and had not turned aside from all which he commanded him.”

verses.zh: 罗波安在世的日子常与耶罗波安争战。
verses.en: Rehoboam[NOTE:1] and Jeroboam were continually at war with each other throughout Abijah’s[NOTE:2] lifetime.
notes: Most Hebrew mss read “Rehoboam”; a few Hebrew mss and the Syriac read “Abijam” (a variant of Abijah).
Heb “his”; the referent (Abijah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 亚比央其余的事，凡他所行的，都写在犹大列王记上。亚比央常与耶罗波安争战。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Abijah’s reign, including all his accomplishments, are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of the Kings of Judah.[NOTE:1] Abijah and Jeroboam had been at war with each other.
notes: Heb “As for the rest of the events of Abijah, and all which he did, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?”

verses.zh: 亚比央与他列祖同睡，葬在大卫的城里。他儿子亚撒接续他作王。
verses.en: Abijah passed away[NOTE:1] and was buried[NOTE:2] in the City of David. His son Asa replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “lay down with his fathers.” The Old Greek also has these words: “in the twenty-eighth year of Jeroboam.”
Heb “and they buried him.”

verses.zh: 以色列王耶罗波安二十年，亚撒登基作犹大王，
verses.en: In the twentieth year of Jeroboam’s reign over Israel, Asa became the king of Judah.

verses.zh: 在耶路撒冷作王四十一年。他祖母名叫玛迦，是押沙龙的女儿。
verses.en: He ruled for 41 years in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] His grandmother[NOTE:2] was Maacah daughter of Abishalom.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “mother,” but Hebrew often uses the terms “father” and “mother” for grandparents and more remote ancestors.

verses.zh: 亚撒效法他祖大卫行耶和华眼中看为正的事，
verses.en: Asa did what the Lord approved[NOTE:1] as his ancestor[NOTE:2] David had done.
notes: Heb “what was right in the eyes of the Lord.”
Heb “father,” but Hebrew often uses the terms “father” and “mother” for grandparents and more remote ancestors.

verses.zh: 从国中除去娈童，又除掉他列祖所造的一切偶像；
verses.en: He removed the male cultic prostitutes from the land and got rid of all the disgusting idols[NOTE:1] his ancestors[NOTE:2] had made.
notes: The word used here, גִלּוּלִים [gillulim], is always used as a disdainful reference to idols. It is generally thought to have originally referred to “dung pellets” (cf. KBL 183 s.v. גִלּוּלִים). It is only one of several terms used in this way, such as “worthless things” (אֱלִילִים, ʾelilim), “vanities” or “empty winds” (הֲבָלִים, havalim).
Heb “fathers” (also in v. 24).

verses.zh: 并且贬了他祖母玛迦太后的位，因她造了可憎的偶像亚舍拉。亚撒砍下她的偶像，烧在汲沦溪边，
verses.en: He also removed Maacah his grandmother[NOTE:1] from her position as queen mother[NOTE:2] because she had made a loathsome Asherah pole. Asa cut down her loathsome pole and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
notes: Heb “mother,” but Hebrew often uses the terms “father” and “mother” for grandparents and more remote ancestors.
The Hebrew term גְּבִירָה (gevirah) can denote “queen” or “queen mother” depending on the context. Here the latter is indicated, since Maacah was the wife of Rehoboam and mother of Abijah.

verses.zh: 只是邱坛还没有废去。亚撒一生却向耶和华存诚实的心。
verses.en: The high places were not eliminated, yet Asa was wholeheartedly devoted to the Lord throughout his lifetime.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “yet the heart of Asa was complete with the Lord all his days.”

verses.zh: 亚撒将他父亲所分别为圣与自己所分别为圣的金银和器皿都奉到耶和华的殿里。
verses.en: He brought the holy items that he and his father had made into the Lord’s temple, including the silver, gold, and other articles.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and he brought the holy things of his father and his holy things (into) the house of the Lord, silver, gold, and items.” Instead of “his holy things,” a marginal reading (Qere) in the Hebrew text has “the holy things of [the house of the Lord].”

verses.zh: 亚撒和以色列王巴沙在世的日子常常争战。
verses.en: Now Asa and King Baasha of Israel were continually at war with each other.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.”

verses.zh: 以色列王巴沙上来要攻击犹大，修筑拉玛，不许人从犹大王亚撒那里出入。
verses.en: King Baasha of Israel attacked Judah and established Ramah as a military outpost to prevent anyone from leaving or entering the land of King Asa of Judah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and he built up Ramah so as to not permit going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.”

verses.zh: 于是亚撒将耶和华殿和王宫府库里所剩下的金银都交在他臣仆手中，打发他们往住大马士革的亚兰王―希旬的孙子、他伯利们的儿子便・哈达那里去，
verses.en: Asa took all the silver and gold that was left in the treasuries of the Lord’s temple and of the royal palace and handed it to his servants. He then told them to deliver it[NOTE:1] to Ben Hadad son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion, king of Syria, ruler in Damascus, along with this message:
notes: Heb “King Asa sent it.”

verses.zh: 说：「你父曾与我父立约，我与你也要立约。现在我将金银送你为礼物，求你废掉你与以色列王巴沙所立的约，使他离开我。」
verses.en: “I want to make a treaty with you, like the one our fathers made.[NOTE:1] See, I have sent you silver and gold as a present. Break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel, so he will retreat from my land.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[May there be] a covenant between me and you [as there was] between my father and your father.”
Heb “so he will go up from upon me.”

verses.zh: 便・哈达听从亚撒王的话，派军长去攻击以色列的城邑；他们就攻破以云、但、亚伯・伯・玛迦、基尼烈全境、拿弗他利全境。
verses.en: Ben Hadad accepted King Asa’s offer and ordered his army commanders to attack the cities of Israel.[NOTE:1] They conquered[NOTE:2] Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maacah, and all the territory of Naphtali, including the region of Kinnereth.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and Ben Hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of the armies which belonged to him against the cities of Israel.”
Heb “he struck down.”
A city in Galilee (Deut 3:17) along with its surrounding region; Kinnereth was also another name for the Sea of Galilee.

verses.zh: 巴沙听见，就停工不修筑拉玛了，仍住在得撒。
verses.en: When Baasha heard the news, he stopped fortifying[NOTE:1] Ramah and settled down in Tirzah.
notes: Heb “building.”

verses.zh: 于是亚撒王宣告犹大众人，不准一个推辞，吩咐他们将巴沙修筑拉玛所用的石头、木头都运去，用以修筑便雅悯的迦巴和米斯巴。
verses.en: King Asa ordered all the men of Judah (no exemptions were granted) to carry away the stones and wood that Baasha had used to build Ramah.[NOTE:1] King Asa used the materials to build up[NOTE:2] Geba (in Benjamin) and Mizpah.
notes: Heb “and King Asa made a proclamation to all Judah, there was no one exempt, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its wood which Baasha had built.”
Heb “and King Asa built with them.”

verses.zh: 亚撒其余的事，凡他所行的，并他的勇力与他所建筑的城邑，都写在犹大列王记上。亚撒年老的时候，脚上有病。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Asa’s reign, including all his successes and accomplishments, as well as a record of the cities he built, are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of the Kings of Judah.[NOTE:1] Yet when he was very old he developed a foot disease.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “As for the rest of all the events of Asa, and all his strength and all which he did and the cities which he built, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Judah?”
Heb “Yet in the time of his old age he became sick in his feet.”

verses.zh: 亚撒与他列祖同睡，葬在他祖大卫城他列祖的坟地里。他儿子约沙法接续他作王。
verses.en: Asa passed away[NOTE:1] and was buried with his ancestors in the city of his ancestor David. His son Jehoshaphat replaced him as king.
notes: Heb “lay down with his fathers.”

verses.zh: 犹大王亚撒第二年，耶罗波安的儿子拿答登基作以色列王共二年，
verses.en: In the second year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Jeroboam’s son Nadab became the king of Israel; he ruled Israel for two years.

verses.zh: 拿答行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，行他父亲所行的，犯他父亲使以色列人陷在罪里的那罪。
verses.en: He did evil in the sight of[NOTE:1] the Lord. He followed in his father’s footsteps and encouraged Israel to sin.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in the eyes of.”
Heb “and he walked in the way of his father and in his sin which he made Israel sin.”

verses.zh: 以萨迦人亚希雅的儿子巴沙背叛拿答，在非利士的基比顿杀了他。那时拿答和以色列众人正围困基比顿。
verses.en: Baasha son of Ahijah, from the tribe of Issachar, conspired against Nadab[NOTE:1] and assassinated him in Gibbethon, which was in Philistine territory. This happened while Nadab and all the Israelite army were besieging Gibbethon.
notes: Heb “against him”; the referent (Nadab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 在犹大王亚撒第三年巴沙杀了他，篡了他的位。
verses.en: Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa’s reign over Judah and replaced him as king.

verses.zh: 巴沙一作王就杀了耶罗波安的全家，凡有气息的没有留下一个，都灭尽了，正应验耶和华藉他仆人示罗人亚希雅所说的话。
verses.en: When he became king, he executed Jeroboam’s entire family.[NOTE:1] He wiped out[NOTE:2] everyone who breathed, in keeping with the Lord’s message that he had spoken through his servant Ahijah the Shilonite.
notes: Heb “house,” meaning “family” by metonymy.
Heb “He did not allow to survive.”

verses.zh: 这是因为耶罗波安所犯的罪使以色列人陷在罪里，惹动耶和华―以色列　神的怒气。
verses.en: This happened because of the sins which Jeroboam committed and which he made Israel commit. These sins angered the Lord God of Israel.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “because of Jeroboam which he committed and which he made Israel commit, by his provocation by which he made the Lord God of Israel angry.”

verses.zh: 拿答其余的事，凡他所行的，都写在以色列诸王记上。
verses.en: The rest of the events of Nadab’s reign, including all his accomplishments, are recorded in the scroll called the Annals of the Kings of Israel.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “As for the rest of the events of Nadab, and all which he did, are they not written on the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?”

verses.zh: 亚撒和以色列王巴沙在世的日子常常争战。
verses.en: Asa and King Baasha of Israel were continually at war with each other.

verses.zh: 犹大王亚撒第三年，亚希雅的儿子巴沙在得撒登基作以色列众人的王共二十四年。
verses.en: In the third year of Asa’s reign over Judah, Baasha son of Ahijah became king over all Israel in Tirzah; he ruled for 24 years.

verses.zh: 他行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，行耶罗波安所行的道，犯他使以色列人陷在罪里的那罪。
verses.en: He did evil in the sight of[NOTE:1] the Lord; he followed in Jeroboam’s footsteps and encouraged Israel to sin.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in the eyes of.”
Heb “and he walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sin which he made Israel sin.”
